newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-Bank of Boston chief's strategy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Bank of Boston chief's strategy.

text.p: Henrique Meirelles, who takes over as Bank of Boston Corp's new president next month, said he is determined to transform the bank into what he calls "one of the world's 10 global financial institutions".
"I think there will be 10 global financial institutions in the world, which will not be necessarily the biggest, but will have a global approach," Meirelles told Reuters in an interview this week.
"My strategy is to position Bank of Boston among these 10 banks within five years," he added.
Bank of Boston's acquisition of BayBanks for $2 billion made it the largest retail bank in New England.
The 50-year-old Meirelles, who for 12 years ran Bank of Boston's Brazilian operation, was promoted to the bank's number two spot in July.
As president and chief operating officer he will be responsible for the day-to-day running of the bank.
He also becomes the highest ranking Brazilian in the international banking community.
Bank of Boston has had a presence in Argentina since 1917 and in Brazil since 1947, Meirelles said. It has also been very active in Chile and Uruguay, with "competitive advantages" in the region.
He said the bank plans to begin developing products to meet Mercosur's regional demands.
"There are companies with a regional approach, with regional cash management needs. We have already been offering regional services for companies in the Mercosur," he said.
Meirelles said the bank also has been active in the trade finance business not only within the Mercosur region but also between Mercosur and Asian countries.
He said the bank is working on ways to facilitate trade between Mercosur countries and China by setting up in Brazil and Argentina the China Trade Desk, with specialists in China and foreign trade.
"Our idea is to offer our expertise since we know Brazil, we are in China, we know the markets," he said.

Under Meirelles'leadership, assets at Bank of Boston's Brazilian operations have grown to $4.8 billion from around $100 million in 1984. Over the last ten years the bank's branch network grew from five to 28 offices and plans are that they should reach 60 branches by the end of the decade.
Meirelles will take over his new post in Boston on October 4.
